title: Twelve spies (Numbers 13–14)
hook: ten see giants and feel like grasshoppers; two see a good land

segments.voice: Yesterday, the priestly blessing: three lines growing toward peace. Your line was the lord bless you and keep you. Who did you say it over? Day four hundred four.
screen: `THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU.`

segments.voice: Twelve men come back from a forty-day scouting trip. Two of them are carrying a pole between them on their shoulders, and hanging from the pole is a single cluster of grapes. One bunch, and it takes a pole and two men. The whole camp crowds around. The land is real, and it's rich. It flows with milk and honey, the scouts say. And then most of them keep talking. But. The cities are walled and huge. The people are strong. And there are giants. We saw them. Next to them, we looked like grasshoppers. Two of the twelve look at the same grapes, the same walls, the same giants, and tell a completely different story.
screen: `ONE CLUSTER, TWO MEN, ONE POLE.` → `MILK AND HONEY. BUT.` → `WE LOOKED LIKE GRASSHOPPERS.`

segments.voice: Here's how the ten put it, in the King James Bible: "we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight." Read that slowly. First, in our own sight. Then, and so we were in their sight. They decided how small they were before anyone else did. And they never actually asked the giants. Caleb, one of the two, quiets the crowd and says: "Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it." Joshua stands with him. Same facts. Different eyes. The ten saw the walls and measured them against themselves. Caleb and Joshua saw the walls and measured them against God, who had opened a sea for them. But the crowd believes the ten. That night they weep. Let's choose a captain and go back to Egypt, they say. They even talk about stoning Caleb and Joshua. And the consequence is heavy: forty years in the wilderness, a year for every day the spies were gone, until that generation has passed. Their children will enter the land they were afraid of. Of all those counted from twenty years old and up, only Caleb and Joshua will walk in. God says of Caleb that he "had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully." Caleb is the quiet hero of this story, and the Bible comes back to him. Forty-five years later, in the book of Joshua, he's eighty-five, still strong, and he asks for the hill country where the giants lived. Today Israel's Ministry of Tourism uses two men carrying the grapes on a pole as its emblem.
screen: `A CLUSTER, AND A BUT.` · `IN OUR OWN SIGHT, GRASSHOPPERS.` · `WE ARE WELL ABLE.` · `FORTY YEARS, A YEAR FOR A DAY.` · then, large: `HE HAD ANOTHER SPIRIT, AND FOLLOWED ME FULLY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: see one challenge Caleb's way. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind something in front of you that feels like a walled city. A hard conversation. An exam. A diagnosis. A job you're not sure you can do. Notice the grasshopper voice: who you think you are next to it. Now look again with Caleb's eyes. Same walls. But what have you already come through? Who's with you? What grapes are hanging from this, what good is on the other side? If you pray, you can measure it against God instead of yourself. The bell holds the time.
Twelve spies. Sent to scout the land: ten came back feeling like grasshoppers, and two, Caleb and Joshua, said, we are well able.
Your line: we're not grasshoppers. Today, when you hear yourself shrink in front of something big, say it under your breath, and take one step toward it. Day four hundred four.

howItsDone: Christians tell the story of the twelve spies to talk about courage and trust in God, and Caleb is held up in sermons and youth programs as a model of wholehearted faith.

original.note: Hebrew: grasshopper, a small leaping insect. The spies use it for how they saw themselves.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about being brave.
what it means: the ten shrank in their own sight first; Caleb and Joshua saw the same walls and measured them against God.
what a scholar hears: 'in our own sight' comes before 'in their sight'; and Caleb's 'another spirit' returns in Joshua 14, at eighty-five.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): 'so heavy it takes two men' (13:23 says only that they bore it between two on a staff) and 'all the adults who left Egypt' (14:29 says those numbered from twenty years old and upward) now follow the text; cut 'a detail people love' and 'many sermons'. Caleb's eighty-five and 'forty and five years' kept because Joshua 14:10, cited, says it.
Joshua 14:10 gives Caleb's age as eighty-five, 'these forty and five years'; confirm.
'Only Caleb and Joshua will walk in' of the adults who left Egypt: Numbers 14:29–30 (twenty years old and upward). Levites are sometimes discussed as exceptions; confirm the simplification.
Israel Ministry of Tourism logo shows two figures carrying grapes on a pole; confirm it is still the emblem.
Original: חָגָב (singular); the text has כַּחֲגָבִים, 'as grasshoppers'. Confirm.
